title: Federated Learning for Cross-Regional Epidemic Forecasting with Asynchronous Outbreaks
abstract: arXiv:2611.14272v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Objective: Epidemic outbreaks are often asynchronous across regions, yet collaborative forecasting is hampered by privacy laws and heterogeneous public health interventions. We developed and evaluated, as a proof of concept, a federated learning (FL) framework for cross-regional COVID-19 forecasting under asynchronous outbreaks among Guangdong, Macau, and Portugal, while maintaining data sovereignty.   Methods: Using daily case data from WHO and China CDC for the three regions, whose outbreaks were asynchronous and interventions heterogeneous, we trained Long Short-Term Memory networks via FL for short-term forecasting, benchmarked against localized and centralized training using Root Mean Square Error, Mean Absolute Error, and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error. translated_title: 面向异步疫情暴发的跨区域流行病预测联邦学习方法
translated_abstract: 目的：疫情暴发在不同地区之间往往是异步发生的，然而隐私法律以及异构的公共卫生干预措施阻碍了协作预测的发展。作为概念验证，我们开发并评估了一个联邦学习（FL）框架，用于在广东、澳门和葡萄牙这三个疫情异步暴发地区之间进行跨区域COVID-19预测，同时保持数据主权。方法：利用世界卫生组织（WHO）和中国疾控中心提供的三个地区的每日病例数据（这些地区的疫情暴发是异步的且干预措施各异），我们通过联邦学习训练长短期记忆（LSTM）网络进行短期预测，并以均方根误差（RMSE）、平均绝对误差（MAE）和对称平均绝对百分比误差（SMAPE）为指标，与本地化训练和集中式训练进行了基准比较。所有实验均使用Flower联邦学习框架，并在各站点间采用一致的超参数。实验使用了公开可得的汇总病例计数数据，以便集中式
tldr: 本文提出并验证了一个基于联邦学习的跨区域COVID-19预测框架，利用LSTM网络在广东、澳门和葡萄牙等疫情异步暴发地区之间进行协作预测，在保持数据主权的同时与本地化及集中式训练方案进行了性能对比。
en_tdlr: This paper develops and evaluates a proof-of-concept federated learning framework that uses LSTM networks for cross-regional COVID-19 forecasting across Guangdong, Macau, and Portugal under asynchronous outbreaks, preserving data sovereignty while benchmarking against localized and centralized training.
